answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring bonded, rate-limited sponsorship. A new sparrow may enter only if an established peer locks a time-delayed stake against that introduction. When later work clusters—shared timing, phrasing, or endpoints—the detection graph sends a ripple through every co-sponsored identity and slashes the bond. Reputation then unfolds like a lotus: spendable rights accrue only after several uncorrelated epochs of countersigned work, so mass-cloned identities never pay.
